text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Friday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
POLITIKA

- Yugoslavia considers normalisation of relations with ex-Yugoslav republics important in its strategy of peace and stabilisation, says President Zoran Lilic in an interview to Nedeljni Dnevnik of Novi Sad.
- Belgrade soccer team Red Star beat Germany's Kaiserslautern 4-0 in a European Cup-Winners Cup match in Belgrade.
- Yugoslav Prime Minister Radoje Kontic to visit Slovakia in earlay October.
- Yugoslavia has ambitious plans for development of telecommunications, says Yugoslav transport and communications minister Zoran Vujovic at a forum in Washington.

- Serbian Deputy Prime Minister Nedeljko Sipovac says the government plans to crop 1,070,000 hectares of land this year, including 830,000 of wheat. It will need to import fertiliser to complete the sowing, he said.

- The Serbian government's plan to lower income taxes and social security benefits, which comes into effect on October 1, will create better conditions for the economy, says Serbian minister coordinator Dragan Tomic.

- Serbia's trade deficit in the first eight months of this year stood at $1.05 billion and prospects of reducing it to the forecast $500 million by year end are small, said Yugoslav trade minister Djordje Siradovic.
- A three-day Poliomyelitis vaccination campaign is starting in central Serbia and Kosovo province.
- The economy in Kosovo province is better than in Serbia and Yugoslavia says president of the Yugoslav Chamber of economy Mihajlo Milojevic in Pec.
- An earthquake measuring 4.6 on the Richter scale was registered 120 kilometers southeast of Belgrade at 22:29 on Thursday without causing any damages.
NASA BORBA
- Former Yugoslav central bank governor Dragoslav Avramovic addresses protesters of Zastava arms in Kragujevac, calling for radical changes in the economy and leadership.
- Avramovic will officially announce on Saturday his decision on whether to head the election list of opposition coalition Zajedno.
- Leader of Serbian Renewal Movement (SPO) Vuk Draskovic addresses letter to Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic asking him to lift his clamp-down on the media.
- Friday's federal parliament session to endorse a number of bilateral agreements, including the Croatian-Yugoslav and the Macedonian-Yugoslav agreements.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Yugoslav Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic expects sanctions against Yugoslavia to be lifted very soon, by Monday or Tuesday next week.
BORBA
- Industrial output in Montenegro in the first eight months of this year is 54.7 percent up on the same period last year, says Montenegrin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic.
